I think this is not needed.
Are you talking about the deferred event or sending the activate fw request?
I've removed the code
This doesn't look like the correct behavior- In this case, PLDM UA won't send UpdateComponent command for the other FD components if ApplyComplete failed for the first component.
In case of failure in applyComplete, we have logic in cancelUpdateComponent() to send the UpdateComponent request to the next component
Done
Can't we have this logic in applyComplete() itself ?
Its present here because we might need to cancel during verify/transfer as well
The commit message could include the high level business logic like CancelUpdate is all components failed vs ActivateFirmware is one component succeeded etc.
Ack I've updated the commit message
nit: send -> Send
Acknowledged
should this be a private method ?
Acknowledged
Why is the componentUpdateStatus at Index 0 updated to true here when the last component is updated?
Yes, this is unnecessary since we don't use the Map again. I've removed the changes
Does this patch introduce support for multiple components update for a device? If so we need to update the commit message.
No, the support for updating multiple components is already present
nit: `cancel update component` -> `CancelUpdateComponent`
Acknowledged

type alias for code readability, also improve the description to include when a component update is marked failed, if there are multiple conditions.

Does `False` indicate component update failed or it is cancelled?

Ack I've added the type alis
False is for when the update is cancelled. I've improved the doxygen comment to reflect the same
If encoding fails, the code continues to send a malformed request. (missing `return` here)
Acknowledged

why `-1` ?
Shouldn't it be `if (cancelledUpdates != applicableComponents.size())`?
The `-1` is to indicate that we're checking if there were any successful component updates not including the current component

Suppose there are two components to update, update was successful on 1st component but it failed for second component.

cancelledUpdates would be 1 

applicableComponents.size() - 1 = 2-1 = 1

This condition would be false in that case, and UA will not send activate firmware request.
Correct me if I am wrong here
Ack, I've updated the logic to make it more straightforward
This resolves the issue
should this be inside an `else` block ?
The update for the device will still be marked as failed even if one of the components has a successful update

But then we are calling updateDeviceCompletion again in activateFirmware and marking it as true.
So we are not actually marking it failed for partial updates here.
Acknowledged
preset it to false instead, it should be marked to true only on success
I don't think it matters what the default value is since we're setting it to the correct value in the failed scenarios
We could have avoided setting it to false in the case of failure, and only set it true for the success cases.
Acknowledged
use placement new rather than reinterpret_cast (There has been a alot of work on this recently in master, please follow the same pattern here as well.)
Acknowledged
